headline: High-risk shared filesystem and server-side code make Langflow→MinerU pair vulnerable to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write uploaded files and server-side flow outputs, while MinerU reads local documents and exposes MCP/API surfaces. A shared workspace or file handoff lets MinerU ingest Langflow-produced content as data, and Langflow can also chain agents. This is plausible in default deployments, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF Langflow writes a document that MinerU later parses from a shared directory
IF an operator bridges the pair through copy-paste or an MCP/file handoff
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Require manual review before MinerU processes Langflow outputs
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and per-flow credentials on a server filesystem; MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text through API/MCP surfaces. If sensitive documents are routed from Langflow into MinerU, both agents can expose the same data class across different storage and processing paths, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded into Langflow and then forwarded to MinerU
IF either deployment logs or persists extracted content outside the intended retention window
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared flow inputs
Turn off verbose logging for document contents
Store outputs in separate retention buckets
Restrict MinerU to non-sensitive documents
requires-engineering: enforce data-class labels across both systems

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write and shell execution, while MinerU is read-only on files but can use MCP and allowlisted network egress. They do not obviously contend for the same mutable resource, yet shared server-side state and concurrent instances make racey overwrites or inconsistent handoffs plausible if both touch the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace
IF Langflow flow nodes and MinerU jobs run concurrently on shared artifacts
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Serialize access to shared files
Make shared artifacts immutable after creation
Avoid concurrent runs on the same directory
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and emit intermediate outputs, while MinerU exposes MCP/API processing that may consume those outputs as authoritative document text. If MinerU acts on Langflow-produced content without verification, errors or injected instructions can cascade into downstream extraction or actions. The interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF MinerU treats Langflow output as trusted input without validation
IF Langflow-generated text is used to drive downstream document actions or routing
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require schema validation on all handoffs
Reject free-form instructions in document payloads
Log and diff every transformed field
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs on a server filesystem, while MinerU is documented as private/offline but still handles document classes like PDFs, DOCX, and OCR text. If regulated data moves from Langflow into MinerU, retention or residency mismatches can arise; the pair lacks documented compliance alignment, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed in Langflow and then exported to MinerU
IF the two deployments have different retention or residency settings
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared flows
Align retention settings before use
Document the data path for audits
Purge temporary artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
